summary: Rebuilt the result from a brand-new source copy and the normalized patch alone. Apply recipe: copy the pristine source, run the repository apply check at root, apply the normalized patch, and hash the result; both the git-form patch and a plain unified fallback applied cleanly and produced a file byte-identical to the tested copy. Differential recipe: load pristine and patched modules in one process and compare structured snapshots over about 5000 fixed and seeded-random headers in strict and permissive modes; about 10000 comparisons produced zero mismatches. An independent native-assert suite covered ordinary pairs, dates, attributes, domain/path behavior, permissive empty names and leading/multiple equals signs, value terminators, control-character rejection, a 20000-character lexical fixture, a 500000-character timing fixture, and 100000 attributes; all corrected assertions passed. The first assertion run failed only because the local test compared the historical default expiry value, the string 'Infinity', strictly against the number Infinity; the failed log was preserved and the parser behavior matched the unpatched parser. A host handoff with the exact payload and evaluation command was written. Evidence is strong local verification; the official external evaluator was not available, so the source case remains officially unverified.
next_hint: Run the official external patch evaluator on the exported payload and inspect its summary. If a hidden functional test fails, add its shape to the preserved differential corpus and localize against the patched copy; do not treat the local pass as an official pass.
